title: EvoWiki: Incremental State Overwriting and Traceable Question Answering for Cross-Meeting Knowledge Evolution

visual_explainer.question: What changes when supersession is resolved incrementally at write time rather than reconstructed only when answering?
visual_explainer.takeaway: EvoWiki keeps one current-valid state per entity-attribute while preserving closed validity intervals, replacement edges, and provenance for historical audit.
visual_explainer.compared_with: An append-only Wiki with the same extraction, entity structure, and reader but without lifecycle invalidation.

analysis.tldr: EvoWiki resolves supersession during incremental construction and preserves a version ledger for later audit. Its cleanest ablation keeps extraction, coreference, entity Wiki, and reader fixed but removes lifecycle invalidation, dropping macro judge accuracy from 60.09 to 51.46. The full package reads more evidence than top-k baselines, traceability is not directly scored, and lifecycle accounting is incomplete.
analysis.problem: Append-only memory can retrieve current and superseded meeting facts together, while snapshot replacement can discard the history needed to audit how a decision changed.
analysis.core_idea: Build entity-attribute version chains incrementally, close the validity interval of replaced facts, expose one current-valid view, retain provenance and replacement edges, then answer through deterministic entity and temporal addressing over the complete Wiki.
analysis.agent_loop: meeting → resolve/corefer/extract → route entity updates → overwrite active state and preserve history → address current/historical state → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: Read bypasses ordinary top-k retrieval and materializes the complete structured Wiki. The matched no-overwrite ablation isolates lifecycle invalidation better than cross-system comparisons, which change evidence exposure, interface, and build cost.
compared_to: RAPTOR, GraphRAG, HippoRAG2, LightRAG, and LogicRAG
analysis.evidence: Full EvoWiki scores 60.09 macro with DeepSeek versus 51.46 without overwrite and 50.37 for the best package baseline. LongMemEval is 61.60 versus 48.50 for LogicRAG; MeetingQA and ELITR gains over full context are only about one point. Build uses 114,016 tokens/project and Read 17,143 tokens/query at 3.60 seconds.
analysis.why_it_matters: Together with StateMem, it shows that retaining history and resolving operative state are separable: validity can be assembled at answer time or materialized incrementally at write time.
limitations: CrossMeet is generated around lifecycle conflicts and favors the encoded failure family.
The complete Wiki exposes about 17K read tokens versus 3.5K for hybrid RAG, so cross-system evidence budgets are unmatched.
Traceability architecture is not validated with provenance precision/recall; judges see only question, reference, and answer.
Build latency, call count, storage, dollars, incremental-update cost, and break-even query count are missing.
Build errors dominate many failures, including extraction omissions and overwrite failures.
